trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting customer data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 48 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's security contact, then the customer administrator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, about 6,900 customers on the standard DPA
clock_starts: Confirmation that customer data was affected (recorded in the incident log)

trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting customer data (some contracts: suspected incident)
deadline: Within 24 hours of confirmation (or of suspicion where the contract says so)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; terms held in the contract obligations register (from 2026-11-30, POAM-012)

trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting customer data
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual. Plan to the 24-hour and 48-hour clocks; the 72-hour clock never sets the plan

trigger: Security incident affecting Conversational AI customer data
deadline: Per each AQ-01 contract (most say without undue delay); counsel checks the register
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer, involving personal information of Florida residents (501.171(1))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; give the customer all information it needs for its own notices
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), which then gives notice under 501.171(3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - worked example of the third-party agent duty; the customer DPA clocks usually come first
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: State service provider and breach notification duties (generic)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days); several states require a service provider to notify the data owner promptly
notify: Data owners (customers) for customer data; affected residents, attorneys general, and consumer reporting agencies where the company owns the data
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; customers' consumers live in every state. Counsel checks each state's definition of personal information against the data elements taken

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company-owned data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company owns (for example, its employees' or marketing contacts' data) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Only for company-owned data, not customer data
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida, where the company is the covered entity
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension applies only to the notice to individuals, never to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity (company-owned data) and 500 or more Florida individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity and more than 1,000 individuals
clock_starts: When notice to more than 1,000 is required

trigger: Company decides individual notice is not required after investigation and consultation with law enforcement
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity

trigger: Disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a written U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Exchange Act registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination (recorded by the General Counsel)

trigger: Information required by Item 1.05 was not determined or was unavailable at filing and later becomes available
deadline: Amend the Form 8-K once the information is determined or becomes available, as counsel advises
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if an Item 1.05 filing was made

trigger: Next annual report
deadline: With the next Form 10-K: describe whether risks from cybersecurity threats, including previous incidents, have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all registrants

citation: Company insider trading policy (supports SEC disclosure rules)
trigger: Severity-1 incident with potential materiality
deadline: At the first disclosure committee meeting
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy

trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to a banking organization customer for 4 or more hours (scheduled, previously communicated maintenance excluded)
deadline: As soon as possible after the company determines the incident meets the trigger
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact at each affected banking customer; if none was provided, the customer's CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider for about 140 banking organization customers; bank-designated contacts on file for 96 (POAM-012)
clock_starts: Determination that covered services are or are likely to be disrupted or degraded for 4 or more hours

obligation: FedRAMP reportable incident communications (Government Edition only)
citation: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026 (definitions FRD-FRI, FRD-IIR, FRD-OIR, FRD-FIR); agency ATO terms
trigger: Incident that affects or is likely to affect the confidentiality or integrity of federal customer data
deadline: Initial, ongoing, and final incident reports to FedRAMP and agency customers under the FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication rules; timing is confirmed in the current rules and agency ATO terms before use (not restated here)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the Government Edition (SYS-03) or its federal customer data is affected

trigger: Incident affecting agency data or service
deadline: Per each agency contract
notify: Agency contracting officers and security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the Government Edition is affected

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company holds federal contracts for the Government Edition; not triggered by this scenario unless such equipment is found

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or data-theft extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. POL-03 4.7 also requires CEO, General Counsel, and insurer approval

trigger: Confirmed criminal intrusion or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable; also serves as the law enforcement consultation for a Florida no-harm determination (501.171(4)(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; recommended

trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The company is above the SBA size standard and in the IT sector, so it would likely be covered

trigger: Significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practicable
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring outside vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: A sub-processor reports an incident affecting company or customer data
deadline: Track the vendor's notice; the company's own customer clocks start when it confirms customer data is affected
notify: Director of Third-Party Risk Management receives; incident commander decides
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and Florida worked example

obligation: SOC 2 service auditor and ISO/IEC 27001 certification body
trigger: Incident affecting the systems described in the SOC 2 report or the ISO/IEC 27001 scope
deadline: Per engagement terms; at the latest during the period's fieldwork
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI by a business associate
deadline: No later than 60 days after discovery

deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination; customers only after 7 full business days post-LE notice (unless urgent/LE directs otherwise)
notify: USSS and FBI via FCC central reporting facility; then customers
